CREATIVE ARTS — TERMLY EXAM #4 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why do we collect only dead or fallen twigs? (1 mark)
   A. Because they are wet
   B. To protect the environment and living trees
   C. Because they are green
   D. Because they are heavier

2. Why must the tin of charcoal stay closed until it is cold? (1 mark)
   A. The charcoal will become white
   B. The charcoal will taste bad
   C. Fresh air can make hot charcoal catch fire
   D. The tin will float

3. What does the drumhead do when it is struck? (1 mark)
   A. It stays completely still
   B. It vibrates and makes the sound
   C. It cools the drum
   D. It holds the drum stand

4. A melodic percussion instrument is one that (1 mark)
   A. can only make one sound
   B. can play different notes to make a tune
   C. has no parts
   D. is always loud

5. A chest pass starts with the ball held at (1 mark)
   A. the ankles
   B. chest height
   C. above the head
   D. behind the back

6. When is an overhead pass most useful? (1 mark)
   A. When shooting from far
   B. When resting
   C. When a defender is standing close
   D. When you are alone on the court

7. What can be used as the core of an improvised macramé ball? (1 mark)
   A. A metal nail
   B. Crumpled paper or old cloth
   C. A glass bottle
   D. A large stone

8. How many players are in a full netball team on the court? (1 mark)
   A. 9
   B. 7
   C. 5
   D. 11

9. When darkening a colour with black, you should add (1 mark)
   A. white first
   B. a whole tin at once
   C. nothing
   D. a little at a time

10. A montage is (1 mark)
   A. a painting with only one colour
   B. a song
   C. a drawing in charcoal
   D. a picture made by joining many cut pieces on a background

11. To paint an object so it looks round, you should (1 mark)
   A. leave it blank
   B. use one flat colour only
   C. paint a lighter tone on the lit side and a darker tone on the shadow side
   D. paint it black

12. In a montage, the subject matter means (1 mark)
   A. the size of the glue pot
   B. the price of the paper
   C. what the montage is about
   D. the colour of the desk

13. Which letter has an ascender? (1 mark)
   A. o
   B. e
   C. a
   D. b

14. How many guide lines are used for practising lettering in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Six
   B. Ten
   C. Two
   D. Four

15. Dictation in music means (1 mark)
   A. writing down a pattern you hear
   B. singing louder
   C. drawing a picture
   D. copying a friend's book

16. How many claps are there in the pattern ta-te ta-te taa (rest)? (1 mark)
   A. Three
   B. Six
   C. Four
   D. Five

17. Hand signs for d, r and m are shown at heights that (1 mark)
   A. go up from d to r to m
   B. stay the same
   C. go down from d to m
   D. are random

18. Stepwise motion means the tune moves (1 mark)
   A. by big jumps
   B. down only
   C. to the next note above or below
   D. only on one note

19. The sol-fa syllable d is pronounced (1 mark)
   A. dee
   B. dah
   C. day
   D. doh

20. Which move skips over a note? (1 mark)
   A. m to r
   B. r to m
   C. d to m
   D. d to r

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. State four rules of netball. (4 marks)

22. Why do we scratch and wet clay before joining pieces? (3 marks)

23. Name the three primary colours. (2 marks)

24. Give three qualities of a neat montage. (3 marks)

25. Describe how to make a value scale strip of orange. (3 marks)

26. How many beats are there in the pattern ta-te ta-te taa taa? Show your working. (3 marks)

27. Explain how to make a shade of green. (2 marks)

28. Why should a composed rhythm be your own idea? (2 marks)

29. Describe how to compose, write and perform an original four-beat rhythmic pattern. (5 marks)

30. Describe three qualities of a good rhythmic pattern. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — TERMLY EXAM #4 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — To protect the environment and living trees
   Cutting living trees harms the environment.

2. C — Fresh air can make hot charcoal catch fire
   Air can make hot charcoal burn, so we wait until it is fully cool.

3. B — It vibrates and makes the sound
   The stretched skin shakes very fast and produces sound.

4. B — can play different notes to make a tune
   Melodic instruments such as the xylophone play notes of different pitch.

5. B — chest height
   A chest pass begins with the ball at chest level.

6. C — When a defender is standing close
   The ball goes over the defender's arms.

7. B — Crumpled paper or old cloth
   Paper or cloth makes a soft core that keeps its shape.

8. B — 7
   A full netball team has seven players on court.

9. D — a little at a time
   Black is strong, so add it in small amounts.

10. D — a picture made by joining many cut pieces on a background
   A montage joins many pictures or pieces to make one whole picture.

11. C — paint a lighter tone on the lit side and a darker tone on the shadow side
   Tones make an object look solid and round.

12. C — what the montage is about
   The subject matter is the theme.

13. D — b
   The stem of b goes up above the small letters.

14. D — Four
   Ascender line, top of small letters, baseline and descender line make four.

15. A — writing down a pattern you hear
   In dictation, the teacher plays or claps and you write it.

16. D — Five
   Ta-te has two, ta-te has two, taa has one, and the rest has none, so five claps.

17. A — go up from d to r to m
   The signs rise as the pitch rises.

18. C — to the next note above or below
   Steps go to a neighbouring note.

19. D — doh
   The syllable d is doh.

20. C — d to m
   Going from d to m skips r.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: No running with the ball; pass or shoot within three seconds; no contact; defenders stand 0.9 metres away; start with a centre pass. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: It makes the surface rough and sticky so the pieces hold together and do not fall off when dry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for scratching, 1 mark for water, 1 mark for the reason.

23. (2 marks)
   Answer: Red, yellow and blue.
   Working / marking points: Award 2 marks for all three, 1 mark for two.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: Clean cut edges, no glue marks, well-overlapped pieces, firmly stuck and a clear title. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: Draw a strip and divide it into five boxes. Mix orange with white for the two light boxes. Paint pure orange in the middle. Mix orange with black for the two dark boxes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the five boxes, 1 mark for light tones, 1 mark for dark tones.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: 4 beats. Ta-te is 1 beat, ta-te is 1 beat, taa is 1 beat and taa is 1 beat, so 1+1+1+1 = 4.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct stage.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: Add a small amount of black to green, and more if needed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for black, 1 mark for adding a little.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: Copying is not fair and honest. Your own idea shows integrity and creativity.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

29. (5 marks)
   Answer: Choose four beats. Fill each with a crotchet, a pair of quavers or a rest. Make sure the pattern has variation and ends on a crotchet. Write it with rhythm names and note symbols. Clap it to a steady beat and improve it after feedback.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for choosing beats, using different values, ending on a long note, writing it and performing it.

30. (3 marks)
   Answer: It has variation of note values, repetition of a group of notes and ends on a long note.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
